checklists.title: Node Graphs / BoardGraph Interface and Binding Feature Test
checklists.description: Concise QA checklist for testing BoardGraph node graph UI features, typed graph schemas, authoring references, integration projection, and binding-style links. Script compilation is intentionally out of scope.
checklists.defaultGuidance: Use a small test board. Treat preview/projection actions as non-destructive until an explicit Apply button is used. Verify nodes, edges, groups, and references remain visible even when optional providers are missing.

sections.title: Access and board lifecycle
sections.guidancePrompt: Confirm board creation, opening, saving, and file-level actions from the interface.

items.label: Open the Board/Node Graph Editor.
items.detail: Use Tools/PungentFunk Utilities/Board & Graph/Board Editor, the Utilities Browser, or a context menu entry if present.

items.label: Create a Freeform Whiteboard board.
items.detail: Confirm the canvas, board list, and inspector populate.

items.label: Create a typed graph template board.
items.detail: Try Dialogue Quest Flow, Behaviour Tree, AI State Machine, Event Sequence, Skill Tree, or Dependency Map if available.

items.label: Rename the board and edit summary/tags.
items.detail: Use the inspector or File/Rename path and confirm metadata updates.

items.label: Save, close, and reopen the board.
items.detail: Nodes, edges, groups, positions, zoom, and metadata should persist.

items.label: Duplicate, copy ID, and delete safely.
items.detail: Delete should require clear intent. Copy ID should place the stable board ID on the clipboard.

items.label: Open Sticky Notes or the Authoring Browser handoff.
items.detail: The handoff should open safely or show a clear missing-provider state.

sections.title: Canvas navigation and layout
sections.guidancePrompt: Check canvas usability before editing graph content.

items.label: Pan and zoom the canvas.
items.detail: Use mouse/trackpad controls and confirm the canvas remains readable.

items.label: Use Fit, Frame, and 100% view actions.
items.detail: Frame should focus the selection or first match where applicable.

items.label: Toggle grid and snap.
items.detail: Snap should align moved nodes/groups to grid increments when enabled.

items.label: Use board list search and Find Content.
items.detail: Search/filter should expose visible state and Frame First Match should move the view to the result.

items.label: Use the node palette filter.
items.detail: Filtering should reduce available node types without losing the selected graph type.

items.label: Resize left and right panels.
items.detail: Splitters should drag intuitively and the canvas should absorb remaining space.

items.label: Check narrow and wide window layouts.
items.detail: Narrow mode may stack panels, but primary canvas and add/select actions should stay reachable.

sections.title: Nodes, groups, and edges
sections.guidancePrompt: Create and manipulate core graph objects using toolbar, canvas, inspector, and context menus.

items.label: Add a node from the toolbar or canvas.
items.detail: Use Add Node, the node type picker, shortcut, or canvas context menu.

items.label: Edit node title, summary, body, and style.
items.detail: Use the inspector. The canvas card should update after editing.

items.label: Move, resize, and collapse a node.
items.detail: Confirm position, size, and collapsed state persist after save/reopen.

items.label: Duplicate and delete a node.
items.detail: Duplication should create a separate ID. Delete should remove connected stale references or report them clearly.

items.label: Add and edit a group.
items.detail: A group is a movable visual container around nodes. Test title, rectangle, style, collapse, and lock where available.

items.label: Move nodes into and out of a group.
items.detail: Contained node counts should update in the inspector or outline.

items.label: Start an edge from one node and connect to another.
items.detail: An edge is a relationship line. Use ports, connector mode, context menu, or inspector buttons.

items.label: Edit edge type, label, direction, and ports.
items.detail: A typed edge should respect graph schema rules and update visually.

items.label: Use multi-select actions.
items.detail: Marquee or shift-select multiple nodes, then copy IDs, duplicate, align, distribute, or delete selection.

sections.title: Typed graph schemas and validation
sections.guidancePrompt: Verify graph type rules, schema fields, and validation feedback.

items.label: Switch graph type and review the node palette.
items.detail: Graph type controls which node types, edge rules, ports, and schema fields are available.

items.label: Create valid nodes for the selected graph type.
items.detail: For example, use state nodes in state-machine mode or behaviour nodes in behaviour-tree mode.

items.label: Attempt an invalid edge connection.
items.detail: The editor should reject it or show a clear validation reason instead of creating a broken edge.

items.label: Edit node schema fields.
items.detail: Schema fields are custom fields required or allowed by a graph type.

items.label: Edit edge schema fields or rule constraints.
items.detail: Confirm directed/undirected and port settings are visible where relevant.

items.label: Run Validate.
items.detail: Validation should group issues clearly, such as schema issues, missing refs, or local data problems.

items.label: Use a Quick Fix only after reading it.
items.detail: Quick Fix should state what it changes and should not silently rewrite unrelated nodes.

items.label: Confirm stale or invalid refs remain visible.
items.detail: Broken refs should show warnings, not disappear from the graph.

sections.title: Authoring references and inspector links
sections.guidancePrompt: Test links from nodes/boards to shared authoring items and external targets.

items.label: Set a linked authoring reference on a node.
items.detail: An authoring reference points to a shared PFU item such as a document, note, data sheet, task, token, or external target.

items.label: Use Set Ref From Node and Match Node To Ref.
items.detail: Set Ref From Node creates/chooses a link; Match Node To Ref copies useful title/summary data from the linked item.

items.label: Open the linked item.
items.detail: Open Linked should open the provider if installed or show a clear disabled/missing package reason.

items.label: Clear a linked reference.
items.detail: Clearing should remove only the link, not delete the linked item or node.

items.label: Add board-level references or targets.
items.detail: Use inspector reference/target controls and verify they persist.

items.label: Copy board, node, edge, and group IDs.
items.detail: IDs should be stable and useful for linking or debugging.

items.label: Check inspector states for selection types.
items.detail: Board, node, edge, group, and multi-selection should each show relevant controls only.

items.label: Confirm missing provider fallback.
items.detail: If a linked document, sheet, or provider is absent, the node should remain visible with safe actions like copy ID/path.

sections.title: Integration profile and projection preview
sections.guidancePrompt: Projection imports authoring/provider data into graph objects. Preview first, then apply selected changes only.

items.label: Create or select an integration profile.
items.detail: A profile stores how external or authoring data should create/update board nodes, edges, and groups.

items.label: Set source filters and provider options.
items.detail: Test provider IDs, kinds, include/exclude types, explicit roots, and cap where available.

items.label: Add selected roots.
items.detail: Explicit roots limit what the projection pulls from; use safe test authoring items.

items.label: Add field mappings.
items.detail: Field mappings copy values from a source key into node or graph fields. Confirm fallback values are visible.

items.label: Add relation mappings.
items.detail: Relation mappings create edges from object refs, paths, or other relationship signals.

items.label: Add group mappings.
items.detail: Group mappings create or update visual groups from provider data.

items.label: Run Preview Import.
items.detail: The preview should list proposed creates, updates, stale marks, skips, and reasons before applying.

items.label: Toggle preview entries before applying.
items.detail: Only selected preview entries should be applied.

items.label: Apply selected projection changes.
items.detail: Confirm created/updated nodes, edges, and groups match the preview.

items.label: Save and reload the profile.
items.detail: Profile settings, mappings, and filters should persist or reset only when Reset Default is used.

sections.title: Persistence, help, and missing states
sections.guidancePrompt: Finish with active UI and recovery checks.

items.label: Use Undo and Redo for graph edits.
items.detail: Move, create, connect, delete, then undo/redo the change.

items.label: Check board outline counts.
items.detail: Outline counts for nodes, edges, and groups should match the canvas.

items.label: Confirm help or checklist buttons open safely.
items.detail: Help, Feature Test Checklist, or Utilities Browser handoffs should open relevant surfaces or calm fallback states.

items.label: Check empty-board and no-selection states.
items.detail: The UI should offer Add Node/Add Group or explain what to select.

items.label: Confirm optional links degrade gracefully.
items.detail: Document/Data Sheet/Audit bridges should be absent or disabled with explanations when not installed.

checklists.title: Rich Documents Interface Feature Test
checklists.description: Concise QA checklist for testing Rich Document Editor UI features, custom insertions, semantic content, annotations, and explicit reference binding. Script compilation is intentionally out of scope.
checklists.defaultGuidance: Work from the visible UI. Mark an item passed only when the control is reachable, visible, usable, and produces the expected state. Use a small test document and a few safe scene/project objects for binding checks.

sections.title: Access and document lifecycle
sections.guidancePrompt: Confirm the editor can be opened, basic document actions work, and saved state is recoverable.

items.label: Open the Rich Document Editor.
items.detail: Use Tools/PungentFunk Utilities/Documentation & Authoring/Rich Document Editor, the Utilities Browser, or the available browser card.

items.label: Create a new document from a template.
items.detail: Use File/New or a template entry and verify the document title/body appear in the editor.

items.label: Edit the title, summary, status, priority, and tags.
items.detail: These metadata fields should save with the document and reappear after reopening.

items.label: Save the document and confirm the saved state.
items.detail: Use Save and check that any save indicator, status pill, or dirty marker clears.

items.label: Reopen the document from Recent or Open.
items.detail: Close or switch away, then reopen the same document and confirm content and metadata persist.

items.label: Duplicate, copy ID, archive, unarchive, and delete safely.
items.detail: Delete/archive actions should require clear intent. Copy ID should place the stable document ID on the clipboard.

items.label: Toggle Document view and Raw Source view.
items.detail: Raw Source is the markup text behind the rendered document. Changes should not silently destroy rendered blocks.

sections.title: Writing and formatting tools
sections.guidancePrompt: Test normal authoring controls before semantic or custom insertions.

items.label: Type plain body text and save it.
items.detail: Add a few lines of prose and verify they render as normal document content.

items.label: Use bold and italic controls.
items.detail: Selected text or inserted markup should render with the intended emphasis.

items.label: Insert H1, H2, and H3 headings.
items.detail: Headings should be visually distinct and should not break surrounding text.

items.label: Insert quote, code block, and divider formats.
items.detail: Use the Formatting menu and confirm each format is readable in the canvas.

items.label: Toggle line numbers and annotation markers.
items.detail: The controls should show/hide markers without changing document content.

items.label: Toggle semantic tint and raw syntax hints.
items.detail: Semantic tint means visual coloring by block type. Raw syntax hints reveal markup clues without replacing the rendered view.

items.label: Insert a token from the token field.
items.detail: A token is a reusable keyed reference such as a variable or content key. Confirm the inserted token is visible and not treated as plain accidental text.

sections.title: Semantic insertions and conversions
sections.guidancePrompt: Verify built-in content blocks are reachable from menus, selections, and context actions.

items.label: Insert a Dialogue/Speaker Line block.
items.detail: Use Insert/Dialogue/Speaker Line and confirm the block is editable and visually distinct.

items.label: Insert a Dialogue Choice or Yarn/Ink option.
items.detail: Confirm choice-style content is rendered as an interactive/semantic row, not just plain text.

items.label: Insert a quest objective and tutorial step.
items.detail: These should appear as purpose-specific semantic blocks with editable fields.

items.label: Insert command placeholder and game-copy blocks.
items.detail: Try Command Placeholder, Hint, Item Description, and Character Description entries.

items.label: Convert selected prose into a semantic block.
items.detail: Select normal text, then use the Properties tray or context menu to convert it to dialogue, choice, quest, tutorial, game copy, or command.

items.label: Use segment context actions.
items.detail: Right-click or use the segment action menu to copy source, add related content, change type, or delete a segment.

items.label: Validate semantic content.
items.detail: Run Validate and confirm warnings are understandable and located near the affected document state.

items.label: Confirm {chip:Name} is not flagged as a bad token.
items.detail: Custom chips use chip syntax. Validation should treat them as Rich Document insertions, not malformed normal tokens.

sections.title: Custom chips and insertion designer
sections.guidancePrompt: Custom insertions are project-defined authoring blocks. Test creation, saving, insertion, and Data Sheet bridge behavior.

items.label: Open Manage Insertions.
items.detail: Use Insert/Custom/Manage Insertions or Advanced/Manage Custom Insertions.

items.label: Create and save a custom chip.
items.detail: A chip is a small inline badge. Set ID/display name/category/tint/default text, save, then reopen the designer.

items.label: Render a custom chip in the document.
items.detail: Type or insert syntax like {chip:Stage Direction}. Confirm it renders as an inline chip.

items.label: Create and save a custom insertion.
items.detail: Add at least two fields and confirm ID/display/category/render mode/validation hint are retained.

items.label: Use the live preview in the designer.
items.detail: The preview should update when labels, field kinds, tint, or defaults change.

items.label: Add a repeatable section.
items.detail: A repeatable section is a group of fields that can be added multiple times, such as list entries or steps.

items.label: Insert the custom insertion from the Insert menu.
items.detail: The saved custom insertion should appear under Custom or its configured category.

items.label: Use + controls on repeatable content.
items.detail: In the document editor, add at least one repeated row/section and verify it saves.

items.label: Convert selected prose to a custom chip or insertion.
items.detail: Use selection/context actions or the Properties tray to convert existing text without leaving the writing flow.

items.label: Test Data Sheet export/import safety.
items.detail: Export definitions if Data Sheets is installed. For import, verify there is a preview/confirmation before definitions are applied.

items.label: Use Copy Definitions As TSV if available.
items.detail: TSV means tab-separated text. Use it as a simple export fallback when the full Data Sheet bridge is unavailable.

sections.title: Properties, annotations, and reference binding
sections.guidancePrompt: Test the side properties surface and explicit object/property binding. Bind only to safe test objects.

items.label: Open and close the Properties tray.
items.detail: The tray should not cover the current editing target and should remember a practical size where supported.

items.label: Add a comment and a bookmark.
items.detail: Create each annotation type and verify it appears in the document or annotation list.

items.label: Edit, re-anchor, and archive an annotation.
items.detail: Re-anchor means move the annotation target to the current text selection.

items.label: Bind an object reference.
items.detail: Use Bind Object on a selected Unity object/component. This should store an explicit reference endpoint, not search the whole project.

items.label: Bind a property endpoint.
items.detail: A property endpoint is a specific field/path on the selected object. Choose one from the picker and bind it.

items.label: Inspect bound reference feedback.
items.detail: The UI should show what object/property is bound and provide clear missing/invalid feedback if the target disappears.

items.label: Open Propagation Preview before applying changes.
items.detail: Propagation means pushing document-linked edits to related targets. The preview should list changes before any apply action.

items.label: Confirm missing providers degrade safely.
items.detail: If Data Sheets, BoardGraph, Tokens, or other providers are absent, linked data should stay visible with disabled actions and clear reasons.

sections.title: Layout, help, and persistence
sections.guidancePrompt: Finish with active UI usability checks instead of compile checks.

items.label: Check narrow, comfortable, and wide window sizes.
items.detail: Core authoring actions should remain reachable. Horizontal scrolling should not be required for normal controls.

items.label: Check short and tall window heights.
items.detail: The document body should scroll intentionally, and primary actions should remain reachable.

items.label: Verify custom definitions persist after reload.
items.detail: Reopen the project or domain reload if practical, then confirm custom chips/insertions still appear.

items.label: Use contextual help.
items.detail: Help should open a relevant topic or a calm fallback, not a generic or broken window.

items.label: Confirm empty states explain the next step.
items.detail: No document, no selection, no provider, and no custom definitions should show helpful next actions.

checklists.title: Data Sheets Interface and Binding Feature Test
checklists.description: Concise QA checklist for testing Data Sheet Editor tables, CSV flows, validation, authoring references, and explicit object/property binding. Script compilation is intentionally out of scope.
checklists.defaultGuidance: Use a small test sheet and safe test objects. Prefer explicit buttons like Import, Pull, Build Preview, and Apply; do not expect broad project scans to run automatically.

sections.title: Access and sheet lifecycle
sections.guidancePrompt: Confirm sheet creation, opening, saving, and sheet-level actions from the visible UI.

items.label: Open the Data Sheet Editor.
items.detail: Use the Tools menu, Utilities Browser, or asset/context menu entry if present.

items.label: Create a blank sheet.
items.detail: Verify a grid, tab, and sheet metadata become visible.

items.label: Create a sheet from a template.
items.detail: Use a provided template and confirm expected starter rows/columns appear.

items.label: Rename the sheet.
items.detail: Use the tab, File menu, or inspector title field and confirm the name updates everywhere.

items.label: Save, close, and reopen the sheet.
items.detail: Rows, columns, values, types, widths, and metadata should persist.

items.label: Duplicate, copy ID, and delete safely.
items.detail: Deletion should require clear intent. Copy ID should place the stable sheet ID on the clipboard.

items.label: Open or create the sheet sticky note.
items.detail: The Sticky/Sheet Sticky action should create or open a linked note without losing sheet data.

sections.title: Grid editing and navigation
sections.guidancePrompt: Exercise normal spreadsheet-style editing before binding or import/export.

items.label: Select a single cell.
items.detail: Click a cell and confirm the selected address/value appears in the formula or inspector area.

items.label: Edit a cell by typing.
items.detail: Enter text, commit it, and confirm the display value updates.

items.label: Use Enter, Tab, and Escape while editing.
items.detail: Enter/Tab should commit and move where supported. Escape should cancel active editing.

items.label: Edit through the formula/value bar.
items.detail: The formula/value bar is the text field for the selected cell raw value.

items.label: Select a rectangular range.
items.detail: Drag or shift-select multiple cells and confirm the range is highlighted.

items.label: Copy and paste a cell range.
items.detail: Paste into a safe area and verify row/column alignment is preserved.

items.label: Clear selected cells.
items.detail: Use Delete, Backspace, Clear, or context menu and confirm only selected cells are cleared.

items.label: Use Fill Down and Fill Right.
items.detail: Copy a source cell value into a vertical or horizontal range.

sections.title: Rows, columns, sorting, and filtering
sections.guidancePrompt: Test row and column controls from toolbars, headers, and context menus.

items.label: Add rows and columns from the toolbar.
items.detail: Use + Row and + Column and verify headers and cell grid expand.

items.label: Add rows or columns from context menus.
items.detail: Try Add Row Above/Below and Add Column Left/Right.

items.label: Rename a column.
items.detail: Use header or inspector rename and confirm the label persists.

items.label: Resize a column.
items.detail: Drag the header edge and confirm the width persists after save/reopen.

items.label: Reorder rows or columns.
items.detail: Drag a row/column if supported and verify values move with the row/column.

items.label: Hide and unhide a row or column.
items.detail: Use inspector or context controls and confirm hidden data is not deleted.

items.label: Sort ascending and descending.
items.detail: Sort a typed column and verify rows remain internally consistent.

items.label: Filter visible rows.
items.detail: Use the filter/search field and confirm the filter state is visible and reversible.

sections.title: Data types, CSV, and validation
sections.guidancePrompt: Confirm typed cells and CSV flows are explicit and reversible.

items.label: Set Text, Number, Boolean, Date, EnumText, and AuthoringReference types.
items.detail: Use column type controls. EnumText means the value should come from a predefined option list.

items.label: Check invalid Number and Date feedback.
items.detail: Enter invalid typed values and confirm validation warns without corrupting the cell.

items.label: Edit a Boolean cell.
items.detail: Confirm true/false or toggle behavior is clear.

items.label: Configure and use EnumText options.
items.detail: Add option values, then confirm the cell editor offers those options.

items.label: Import CSV as a new sheet.
items.detail: CSV means comma-separated text. Choose first-row-header and mapping options before importing.

items.label: Append CSV into the current sheet.
items.detail: Use append mode and verify new rows are added without replacing unrelated data.

items.label: Export CSV with visible/display options.
items.detail: Try visible columns only, include hidden rows, and display/raw value settings.

items.label: Run Validate and read the issue summary.
items.detail: Validation should list sheet, type, authoring reference, and binding issues with clear status.

sections.title: Inspector and authoring references
sections.guidancePrompt: Use the inspector to verify metadata, selected row/column/cell state, and shared authoring links.

items.label: Edit sheet metadata in the Selection inspector.
items.detail: Update title, summary, status, priority, visibility, tags, archived, and developer-only flags where available.

items.label: Edit row metadata.
items.detail: Update row display name, order, hidden/locked state, tags, and linked authoring reference.

items.label: Edit column metadata.
items.detail: Update display name, type, width, hidden/locked state, enum options, and column reference.

items.label: Edit raw and display cell values.
items.detail: Raw value is stored data; display value is what the grid shows after formatting/type handling.

items.label: Create an AuthoringReference cell.
items.detail: AuthoringReference means a cell links to another PFU authoring item, such as a note, document, board, or token.

items.label: Use raw authoring link format.
items.detail: Try provider|kind|id|label, then Use Raw As Link. Confirm the link preview updates.

items.label: Write a selected authoring link back to raw value.
items.detail: Use Write Link To Raw and confirm the encoded value is readable.

items.label: Open or preview a linked authoring item.
items.detail: If the provider is missing, the link should remain visible with disabled actions and a clear reason.

sections.title: Object and property binding
sections.guidancePrompt: Bind sheet rows/columns to explicit Unity objects and properties, then preview before applying.

items.label: Create or select a binding profile.
items.detail: A binding profile stores how sheet rows map to Unity objects and properties.

items.label: Choose a target source.
items.detail: Test CurrentSelection, ManualObjects, or AssetFolder depending on what is available.

items.label: Add the current selection as binding targets.
items.detail: Select safe test objects/assets, then use Add Selection. Cached targets should appear.

items.label: Refresh an asset folder target explicitly.
items.detail: Folder refresh should run only after you click Refresh Folder, not on every repaint.

items.label: Map columns to property paths.
items.detail: A SerializedProperty path is Unity’s field path, such as m_Name or a custom serialized field.

items.label: Use pull/apply toggles per column.
items.detail: P means pull values from target to sheet. A means allow applying sheet values back to the target.

items.label: Pull values from targets.
items.detail: Rows should populate or update based on cached targets and mapped columns.

items.label: Build Apply Preview before applying.
items.detail: The preview should show target, property, old value, new value, status, and reason.

items.label: Apply only ready preview entries.
items.detail: Apply should require confirmation and should skip unsupported, locked, missing, or invalid paths safely.

sections.title: Layout, tabs, and missing states
sections.guidancePrompt: Finish with active UI usability checks.

items.label: Resize the inspector/details panel.
items.detail: The splitter should drag intuitively and clamp instead of crushing the grid.

items.label: Switch between multiple sheet tabs.
items.detail: Tabs should remain visible or scroll intentionally when many sheets are open.

items.label: Check narrow, comfortable, and wide sizes.
items.detail: Toolbar, grid, inspector, and bottom tabs should remain usable.

items.label: Check empty and no-selection states.
items.detail: The UI should offer clear actions such as Create Sheet, Import CSV, or select a cell.

items.label: Confirm missing targets/providers are non-breaking.
items.detail: Missing objects, authoring providers, or optional bridges should show disabled actions with explanations, not hidden data.

checklists.title: Environment Simulation/Environment Simulation Workbench
checklists.description: Tests the central scene-level Environment Simulation hub, health summaries, integration opportunities, quick preview controls, and focused-window handoffs.
checklists.defaultGuidance: Mark Pass only when the control is reachable, visible, usable, and produces the expected scene or asset state. Mark Partial when source exists but UI, persistence, layout, or runtime hookup still needs polish.

sections.title: Access, registration, and shared chrome
sections.guidancePrompt: Validate that the hub is reachable through all intended access surfaces before testing deeper workflows.

items.label: Open the tool from the Tools menu.
items.detail: Use Tools/PungentFunk Utilities/Environment Simulation and confirm the expected window opens without console errors.

items.label: Open the tool from the Utilities Browser card.
items.detail: Search for the utility by name and by keywords such as environment, weather, clock, or delta time. Confirm the card opens the same active window.

items.label: Open contextual help from the window header.
items.detail: Use the help affordance in the shared header and confirm the relevant help topic opens rather than a generic or missing topic.

items.label: Open the Layout QA window from the Environment Simulation menu.
items.detail: Confirm Layout QA opens and can launch Hub, Calendar, Weather, and Delta windows at Narrow, Medium, Wide, Short, and Tall sizes.

items.label: Confirm related utility links are surfaced.
items.detail: In the Utilities Browser card or related utility metadata, confirm Calendar Clock, Weather Utility, and Delta Time Controller are discoverable from the Environment Simulation hub entry.

sections.title: Scene discovery and controller creation
sections.guidancePrompt: Start from a scene with no environment controllers, then a scene with all controllers present.

items.label: Refresh finds existing scene controllers.
items.detail: Add or select a scene containing PungentClockController, PungentWeatherController, and PungentDeltaTimeController. Click Refresh and confirm all three system cards change to Found.

items.label: Create missing Calendar Clock from the hub.
items.detail: In an empty scene, use the Calendar Clock system card Create action. Confirm a new scene GameObject with PungentClockController is created and then detected by Refresh.

items.label: Create missing Weather from the hub with output applier.
items.detail: Use the Weather system card Create action. Confirm the created object has PungentWeatherController and the optional PungentWeatherOutputApplier component.

items.label: Create missing Delta Time from the hub.
items.detail: Use the Delta Time system card Create action. Confirm a PungentDeltaTimeController is created, selectable, and shown in the system summary.

items.label: Select buttons focus the correct scene object.
items.detail: For each found card, click Select and confirm Unity Selection changes to the matching controller object.

sections.title: Health cards and optional integration opportunities
sections.guidancePrompt: Use partially configured scenes to verify warnings, ready counts, and optional package hints.

items.label: System and profile count pills update correctly.
items.detail: With 0, 1, 2, and 3 systems configured, confirm Systems, Profiles, and Unity Writers count pills reflect the actual scene/profile state.

items.label: Calendar and sky output health cards explain missing setup.
items.detail: Remove or assign calendarProfile and skyProfile on the clock. Confirm health cards switch between actionable warning and ready states.

items.label: Weather profile, output, and forecast health cards respond to setup.
items.detail: Assign a Weather Profile, add/remove Output Applier, and generate/clear forecast entries. Confirm each health card updates after Refresh.

items.label: Delta profile and Unity time writer status is understandable.
items.detail: Assign a Delta Time Profile and toggle applyToUnityTimeScale on profile channels. Confirm the Unity Writers count reflects channels that write to Unity time.

items.label: Optional package opportunities are calm and non-breaking.
items.detail: Check Timeline, URP, Shader Graph, Terrain Tools, Input System, and Test Framework opportunity cards. Missing packages should show explanatory disabled/fallback states, not errors.

sections.title: Quick preview workflow
sections.guidancePrompt: These are the controls likely to be revisited during design iteration; verify they stay visible and safe.

items.label: Set clock hour from the hub.
items.detail: Use Clock Hour and Set. Confirm the clock Snapshot/inspector time changes immediately and Undo can revert the change.

items.label: Advance Day updates calendar state.
items.detail: Click Advance Day and confirm date, weekday/day-of-year, and season data update appropriately.

items.label: Regenerate Forecast creates a 24-hour forecast.
items.detail: Click Regenerate Forecast and confirm the Weather Controller forecast contains 24 hourly entries and the current state updates.

items.label: Pause and Resume modify the Global pause stack.
items.detail: Click Pause, then Resume. Confirm Global pause stack increments and decrements without going negative.

items.label: Apply Gameplay Scale changes the Gameplay channel only.
items.detail: Set a slow-motion Gameplay scale and Apply. Confirm Gameplay changes while unrelated channels remain unchanged unless profile settings say otherwise.

items.label: Restore resets delta-time defaults.
items.detail: After changing scales and pauses, click Restore. Confirm scales return to profile defaults and pause stacks clear.

sections.title: Layout, resizing, and no-hidden-functionality check
sections.guidancePrompt: Use the Layout QA window and manual docking to check the workflow-first minimal surface pass.

items.label: Narrow layout remains usable.
items.detail: Open the hub at Narrow size. Confirm toolbar buttons wrap or remain reachable, health cards are readable, and only necessary vertical scrolling appears.

items.label: Wide layout does not create dead space or clipped cards.
items.detail: Open at Wide size. Confirm system cards, health cards, and quick preview controls use available width cleanly.

items.label: Short layout keeps frequent preview controls reachable.
items.detail: Dock or resize the hub short. Confirm Refresh and focused-window handoffs remain visible and the quick preview section can be reached without horizontal scrolling.

items.label: Status text updates without layout jumps.
items.detail: Click Refresh and create/select systems. Confirm status text changes but does not push key buttons off-screen.

checklists.title: Environment Simulation/Calendar Clock
checklists.description: Tests the focused Calendar Clock authoring workflow: calendar profile, runtime clock progression, date/time controls, sky output, sequence rules, Timeline bridge, and responsive layout.
checklists.defaultGuidance: Mark Pass only when the control is reachable, visible, usable, and produces the expected scene or asset state. Mark Partial when source exists but UI, persistence, layout, or runtime hookup still needs polish.

sections.title: Access and setup
sections.guidancePrompt: Confirm the focused window, inspector, and scene controller setup are all reachable.

items.label: Open the tool from the Tools menu.
items.detail: Use Tools/PungentFunk Utilities/Environment Simulation and confirm the expected window opens without console errors.

items.label: Open the tool from the Utilities Browser card.
items.detail: Search for the utility by name and by keywords such as environment, weather, clock, or delta time. Confirm the card opens the same active window.

items.label: Open contextual help from the window header.
items.detail: Use the help affordance in the shared header and confirm the relevant help topic opens rather than a generic or missing topic.

items.label: Create or select a PungentClockController from the Calendar window.
items.detail: Open Calendar Clock with no selected clock and use the create/select workflow. Confirm the left setup rail resolves to the created/selected controller.

items.label: Create or assign a Calendar Profile.
items.detail: Use the profile object field/create helper. Confirm the asset is created, assigned, serialized, and visible in the controller inspector.

sections.title: Calendar profile authoring
sections.guidancePrompt: These controls are mostly design-once/touch-up-later; verify they are available but not crowding the frequent controls.

items.label: Edit month names, days, seasons, sunrise, and sunset.
items.detail: Select multiple months in the detail rail and modify name, days, season, sunriseHour, sunsetHour, and seasonalSunTilt. Confirm changes persist on the Calendar Profile asset.

items.label: Date normalization handles month/day overflow safely.
items.detail: Set the clock to an invalid or edge date through the window or inspector, such as day beyond the selected month. Confirm NormalizeDate clamps/rolls to a valid date without exceptions.

items.label: Weekday and day-of-year calculations are believable.
items.detail: Change firstDayOfYear and month lengths. Verify DateLabel, weekday, and dayOfYear update consistently when advancing days.

items.label: Season changes trigger at the expected month boundaries.
items.detail: Advance across months with different season labels and confirm Snapshot.seasonName and season events update when the season changes.

sections.title: Runtime clock and frequent preview controls
sections.guidancePrompt: These controls are likely to be used repeatedly while designing events, sequences, and progression.

items.label: Set Hour updates the current clock snapshot.
items.detail: Use the timeline/workspace hour control and Set. Confirm TimeLabel24, dayPercent, sun/moon output, and OnTimeChanged respond.

items.label: Advance Day updates date and events.
items.detail: Advance one day and confirm OnDayChanged fires, DateLabel changes, and weather systems listening to day change can respond if assigned.

items.label: Reset returns to configured start date/time.
items.detail: Change date/time, click Reset, and confirm the controller returns to startYear/startMonthIndex/startDayOfMonth/startHour.

items.label: Run On Start and IsRunning behavior is clear.
items.detail: Enter Play Mode with runOnStart on/off and confirm time progresses only when intended.

items.label: Clock Delta Time channel affects time progression.
items.detail: Assign a Delta Time Controller and use the Clock channel scale/pause. Confirm clock progression speeds up, slows, or freezes according to the channel.

sections.title: Sky, light, Timeline, and sequence outputs
sections.guidancePrompt: Verify optional outputs can be added and are explicit when missing.

items.label: Clock Sky Profile applies ambient, fog, sun, and moon outputs.
items.detail: Assign sun/moon transforms and lights plus a Clock Sky Profile. Scrub the hour and confirm light rotation/intensity/color and RenderSettings outputs change.

items.label: Missing sky outputs are treated as optional.
items.detail: Remove sun/moon references and skyProfile. Confirm the UI explains optional output state and the controller does not throw runtime errors.

items.label: Create and test a Time Sequence Rule.
items.detail: Create a PungentTimeSequenceRule for a specific hour/date/season. Attach a listener and confirm it fires when the clock reaches the target.

items.label: Skipped-time behavior is understandable.
items.detail: Advance hours across a sequence trigger. Confirm whether missed events fire or do not fire according to the listener/controller settings and note any mismatch.

items.label: Timeline Clock Bridge drives time-of-day from PlayableDirector.
items.detail: Add the bridge from the Calendar window, assign a PlayableDirector, scrub or play it, and confirm clock hour maps between startHour and endHour.

sections.title: Layout and inspector validation
sections.guidancePrompt: Confirm the focused Calendar Clock workflow remains readable in all intended contexts.

items.label: Timeline/day band remains the primary workspace.
items.detail: At Medium and Wide sizes, confirm the day band/timeline is visually dominant and setup/detail rails do not crowd it.

items.label: Narrow layout stacks setup, timeline, and details cleanly.
items.detail: Open at Narrow size and confirm no horizontal scroll is needed for month cards, timeline controls, or detail tabs.

items.label: Custom inspector exposes essential clock actions.
items.detail: Select the PungentClockController and confirm Hub, Set Hour, Advance Day, Reset, profile fields, events, and advanced sections are available and not duplicated confusingly.

items.label: Window preferences persist across reopen.
items.detail: Change selected month/detail tab or rail widths, close and reopen. Confirm useful state persists or resets intentionally without losing assigned scene references.

checklists.title: Environment Simulation/Weather Utility
checklists.description: Tests weather preset authoring, forecast generation, hourly overrides, output routing, volume binding, optional environment effects, and layout behavior.
checklists.defaultGuidance: Mark Pass only when the control is reachable, visible, usable, and produces the expected scene or asset state. Mark Partial when source exists but UI, persistence, layout, or runtime hookup still needs polish.

sections.title: Access and setup
sections.guidancePrompt: Confirm the Weather Utility can be opened, create/selects the controller, and exposes the preset/forecast/detail workflow.

items.label: Open the tool from the Tools menu.
items.detail: Use Tools/PungentFunk Utilities/Environment Simulation and confirm the expected window opens without console errors.

items.label: Open the tool from the Utilities Browser card.
items.detail: Search for the utility by name and by keywords such as environment, weather, clock, or delta time. Confirm the card opens the same active window.

items.label: Open contextual help from the window header.
items.detail: Use the help affordance in the shared header and confirm the relevant help topic opens rather than a generic or missing topic.

items.label: Create or select a PungentWeatherController.
items.detail: Open the Weather Utility with no selected weather controller. Use create/select actions and confirm the controller appears in the scene and detail rails.

items.label: Create or assign a Weather Profile.
items.detail: Use the weatherProfile object field/create helper. Confirm the profile asset is created, assigned, serialized, and visible in the inspector.

items.label: Clock link regenerates daily forecast when intended.
items.detail: Assign a PungentClockController and enable day-change regeneration if available. Advance the clock day and confirm the forecast updates or the missing-link state is clearly explained.

sections.title: Weather preset authoring
sections.guidancePrompt: These controls are mostly design-once/touch-up-later; verify complete authoring and filtering before runtime preview.

items.label: Preset browser lists and filters presets.
items.detail: Create several presets, then use search, precipitation-only, and advanced filters. Confirm matching preset cards remain readable and selectable.

items.label: Basic preset fields affect generated states.
items.detail: Edit displayName, weight, season, temperature range, precipitation chance, cloud cover, fog, wind, wetness, and snow. Generate a forecast and confirm states reflect the ranges.

items.label: Advanced output fields are visible and persist.
items.detail: Edit advanced cloud/volume/terrain-shadow/sky/fog/wind values where present. Confirm they serialize on the Weather Profile asset and are not hidden behind stale UI.

items.label: Preset weighting and seasonal requirements influence forecast selection.
items.detail: Create high-weight and low-weight presets with different seasons. Generate multiple forecasts in different seasons and confirm selection feels plausible.

items.label: Preview Selected Preset updates CurrentState and outputs.
items.detail: Select a preset and use Preview. Confirm CurrentState changes and any assigned output applier receives the preview state.

sections.title: Forecast timeline and hourly editing
sections.guidancePrompt: These controls are likely to be used repeatedly while designing events, sequences, and progression.

items.label: Generate Forecast creates 24 hourly entries.
items.detail: Click Generate Forecast and confirm entries 00:00 through 23:00 exist, are selectable, and have readable names/metrics.

items.label: Current weather interpolates according to clock hour.
items.detail: Assign a clock, scrub hour across adjacent forecast entries, and confirm CurrentState transitions smoothly or as documented.

items.label: Selecting an hour shows editable details.
items.detail: Click multiple forecast hours and confirm the selected-hour editor updates with the correct state values.

items.label: Manual hourly override changes the selected hour.
items.detail: Edit a selected hour or set hourly weather manually. Confirm the hour changes and the override state is visible after refresh.

items.label: Regeneration behavior for manual overrides is explicit.
items.detail: After creating an override, regenerate the forecast. Confirm overrides are preserved or intentionally cleared with clear UI messaging.

sections.title: Output routing, shaders, volumes, particles, audio, and wind
sections.guidancePrompt: Verify optional outputs are safe when missing and useful when assigned.

items.label: Add Output Applier from the Weather Utility.
items.detail: Use Add Output Applier. Confirm the component is added, assigned to the controller, and visible in the output section.

items.label: Fog and RenderSettings outputs update from weather.
items.detail: Enable fog output, preview a foggy preset, and confirm RenderSettings fog state/color/density change as expected and can be disabled safely.

items.label: Shader global outputs are written when enabled.
items.detail: Enable shader global output and preview weather states. Confirm expected wetness/snow/cloud/wind global values are set without material-specific compile dependencies.

items.label: Precipitation particles and ambient audio respond to state.
items.detail: Assign rain/snow particles and ambient audio. Preview clear, rainy, and snowy states and confirm emission/audio intensity responds.

items.label: Volume adapter binds weather metrics into profile floats.
items.detail: Add Volume Adapter, assign a profile, create bindings for cloud/fog/wetness/snow/wind metrics, and confirm Apply updates the targeted float parameters.

items.label: Wind output path is documented or available.
items.detail: Check whether wind outputs are only stored in WeatherState, sent through shader globals, or routed to a generic WindZone/receiver. Mark Partial if generic wind adapters are still absent.

sections.title: Layout and inspector validation
sections.guidancePrompt: Confirm the Weather Utility uses a forecast-first workflow without hiding preset or output controls.

items.label: Forecast workspace remains primary at practical sizes.
items.detail: At Medium/Wide sizes, confirm the forecast timeline is central while preset browser and details are secondary but reachable.

items.label: Narrow layout remains usable for preset cards and forecast hours.
items.detail: Open at Narrow size. Confirm preset cards, forecast hour buttons, selected-hour editor, and output controls do not clip or require horizontal scrolling.

items.label: Custom inspector exposes essential weather actions.
items.detail: Select PungentWeatherController and confirm Hub, Generate Forecast, Preview Preset, profile/output fields, events, and advanced sections are available.

items.label: Missing optional output components are explained calmly.
items.detail: Remove output applier and volume adapter. Confirm the UI shows Add actions or optional-state messaging rather than warnings that imply required setup.

checklists.title: Environment Simulation/Delta Time Controller
checklists.description: Tests delta-time channel profiles, pause stacks, scale blending, Unity Time integration, PlayableDirector adapter, scenarios, and layout behavior.
checklists.defaultGuidance: Mark Pass only when the control is reachable, visible, usable, and produces the expected scene or asset state. Mark Partial when source exists but UI, persistence, layout, or runtime hookup still needs polish.

sections.title: Access and setup
sections.guidancePrompt: Confirm the Delta Time Controller can be opened, created, selected, and configured from focused and inspector surfaces.

items.label: Open the tool from the Tools menu.
items.detail: Use Tools/PungentFunk Utilities/Environment Simulation and confirm the expected window opens without console errors.

items.label: Open the tool from the Utilities Browser card.
items.detail: Search for the utility by name and by keywords such as environment, weather, clock, or delta time. Confirm the card opens the same active window.

items.label: Open contextual help from the window header.
items.detail: Use the help affordance in the shared header and confirm the relevant help topic opens rather than a generic or missing topic.

items.label: Create or select a PungentDeltaTimeController.
items.detail: Open Delta Time with no selected controller and create/select one. Confirm the scene object is created and the window binds to it.

items.label: Create or assign a Delta Time Profile.
items.detail: Use the profile object field/create helper. Confirm default channels are present and profile assignment persists.

items.label: Singleton claim behavior is safe.
items.detail: Place one or more controllers with claimSingleton enabled/disabled. Confirm Instance ownership is predictable and no unexpected duplicate warnings/errors occur.

sections.title: Channel profile authoring
sections.guidancePrompt: These settings are mostly design-once/touch-up-later; verify they are complete and correctly bounded.

items.label: Default channels exist and rebuild correctly.
items.detail: Open a fresh Delta Time Profile and confirm Global, Gameplay, UI, Physics, Animation, Audio, Particles, Clock, Weather, and Custom support are present as expected.

items.label: Minimum/maximum scale clamps are respected.
items.detail: Set scales below minimum and above maximum from the window/API. Confirm the controller clamps to profile bounds.

items.label: Blend duration controls smooth scale transitions.
items.detail: Set a non-zero blendDuration, change a channel scale, and confirm current scale transitions over time rather than snapping unless duration is zero.

items.label: applyToUnityTimeScale controls Unity Time writing.
items.detail: Toggle applyToUnityTimeScale on channels and confirm Time.timeScale/fixedDeltaTime are written only by intended channels.

items.label: Priority and blend update mode behavior is verified.
items.detail: Change priority and blendUpdateMode and test whether they affect runtime behavior. Mark Partial if the fields are serialized but not yet consumed by the controller.

sections.title: Runtime control, pause stacks, and scenarios
sections.guidancePrompt: These controls are likely to be revisited often while tuning pause, slow motion, fast-forward, and sequence previews.

items.label: Set Scale changes the selected channel.
items.detail: Select Gameplay, Clock, Weather, and a Custom channel if configured. Set different scales and confirm GetScale returns the expected current/target values.

items.label: Pause, Pop, and Clear modify pause stacks safely.
items.detail: Push multiple pauses, pop them one at a time, and clear. Confirm stacks never go negative and scale reaches zero only while paused.

items.label: Global Pause and Resume affect Unity-time systems as intended.
items.detail: Use command strip Global Pause/Resume. Confirm pause stack, effective scale, and Unity Time behavior match the profile.

items.label: Scenario buttons apply expected presets.
items.detail: Use Gameplay Slow Motion, Clock Freeze, Weather Fast Forward, and Restore. Confirm each targets the correct channel without unintended side effects.

items.label: Reset All restores profile defaults.
items.detail: After changing multiple channels and pause stacks, click Reset All and confirm channel scales and stacks return to defaults.

sections.title: Adapters and consumers
sections.guidancePrompt: Verify opt-in integrations receive channel scales without forcing generic package dependencies.

items.label: Add PlayableDirector Adapter from the selected channel.
items.detail: Add the adapter, assign a PlayableDirector, select a channel, and confirm playback/root playable speed follows the channel scale.

items.label: PlayableDirector pause/resume behavior is clear.
items.detail: Set the selected channel to zero and then above zero. Confirm pauseDirectorWhenScaleIsZero behavior is predictable and resume behavior is documented.

items.label: Clock consumes the Clock channel.
items.detail: Assign the Delta Time Controller to the Clock Controller and pause/scale the Clock channel. Confirm clock progression responds.

items.label: Weather consumes the Weather channel.
items.detail: Assign the Delta Time Controller to the Weather Controller and scale Weather. Confirm forecast interpolation/current state timing responds if implemented.

items.label: Non-implemented channels are clearly opt-in.
items.detail: Check UI/Physics/Animation/Audio/Particles channels. Mark Pass if they are clearly available as channels and Partial if generic adapters/receivers are still absent but needed.

sections.title: Lifecycle, layout, and safety
sections.guidancePrompt: Confirm the controller is safe to use during editor/play iteration and the focused window remains readable.

items.label: Destroy/disable restores Unity Time safely.
items.detail: While applyUnityTimeScale is active and scale is not 1, disable or destroy the controller. Confirm Time.timeScale and Time.fixedDeltaTime are restored or mark Partial if restoration is not implemented.

items.label: Domain reload/play-mode transitions do not leave stale pause or scale state.
items.detail: Enter/exit Play Mode after pausing or slowing time. Confirm state resets or persists only as intended.

items.label: Channel console is primary and readable.
items.detail: At Medium/Wide sizes, confirm channel rows/cards show scale, pause stack, Set/Pause/Pop/Clear actions, and selected-channel details without clipping.

items.label: Narrow layout wraps channel controls and scenarios cleanly.
items.detail: Open at Narrow size and confirm no horizontal scrolling is required for channel cards, scenario buttons, or detail controls.

items.label: Custom inspector exposes essential delta-time actions.
items.detail: Select PungentDeltaTimeController and confirm Hub, Set Gameplay Scale, Pause/Resume/Reset, profile fields, events, and advanced sections are available.

checklists.title: Texture Generation Systems QA Checklist
checklists.description: Importable QA checklist for the current PungentFunk Utilities Texture Generator / Texture Designer systems, including workflow routing, manual composition, guided generation, influence diagrams, seamless texture support, export, persistence, and performance validation.
checklists.defaultGuidance: Use Pass only when the feature is implemented in source, reachable in the active Unity UI, visible at usable sizes, and behaves as expected. Use Partial for incomplete or unclear behavior. Use Fail for missing, unreachable, broken, or compile-blocking behavior. Add notes with exact file/control/Unity Console details.
checklists.sourceLabel: Generated from current uploaded PungentFunkUtilities.zip audit

sections.title: Setup, compile, and access
sections.guidancePrompt: Resolve compile/access failures before testing UI behavior.

items.label: Project compiles with the uploaded Texture Designer scripts.
items.detail: Open Unity and confirm there are no Console compile errors. Pay special attention to Procedural Texture Lab partial classes and runtime/editor assembly separation.

items.label: Texture Generator opens from its intended menu or Utilities Browser card.
items.detail: Verify the window title, shared PFU header, status text, Help/context affordance if present, and stable access path.

items.label: Utilities Browser entry is accurate and package-owned.
items.detail: Confirm the utility card name/description/category/ownership indicate Appearance / Colour / Texture or the current intended package, without Core-only misclassification.

items.label: Fresh session has a useful empty state.
items.detail: Clear saved prefs/session if needed, reopen the window, and confirm the empty workbench explains how to start without a wall of fields.

items.label: Window survives domain reload and reopen.
items.detail: Open the tool, generate at least one variant, switch panels/workflows, trigger script reload/domain reload, then reopen and verify state is sane.

sections.title: Shared shell, layout, and responsive behavior
sections.guidancePrompt: Test whether the tool remains usable at practical docked and floating sizes.

items.label: Header and toolbar remain compact and readable.
items.detail: Check Generate/Stop, Randomize/Mutation, Guide/Lock equivalent, Inspector, View, Save/Export actions, and tooltips at normal width.

items.label: Narrow docked width remains usable.
items.detail: Resize near minimum width. Frequent controls should wrap, compact, or move to clear dropdowns; no critical action should become unreachable.

items.label: Wide window uses space effectively.
items.detail: Resize wide. The preview/workbench should expand rather than leaving large dead gaps or over-compressing the inspector.

items.label: Short window height preserves primary actions.
items.detail: Reduce height. Primary generation/refine/export actions should remain reachable without excessive scroll traps.

items.label: Inspector popup/inline behavior is usable.
items.detail: Toggle the inspector at widths below and above inline threshold. Check resize handle, popup placement, close behavior, and persistence.

items.label: View popup behaves as a compact surface.
items.detail: Open View. Check Escape/outside-click behavior, tile/checkerboard/density controls, tooltips, and that values visibly affect the workbench.

sections.title: Phase tabs and workflow routing
sections.guidancePrompt: These items validate the workflow-first Texture Designer direction; fail them if the active UI still always routes to the candidate grid.

items.label: Compose phase is visible and selected by default.
items.detail: Confirm Compose is an explicit phase/tab or clearly equivalent primary surface.

items.label: Refine phase has an active workbench, not only inspector fields.
items.detail: Switch to Refine and confirm the central workbench changes to a focused preview/refine layout with candidate strip or equivalent.

items.label: Export phase has an active export/map workbench.
items.detail: Switch to Export and confirm map toggles/previews/export actions are visible in the central workflow or a clearly reachable surface.

items.label: History phase is reachable and useful.
items.detail: Switch to History and verify snapshots/history entries can be reviewed, restored, and reused.

items.label: Compose has a Workflow selector.
items.detail: Look for Manual Compose, Random Explore, Guided Refine, Blend Lab, Reference Match, Constraint Match, Preset Browser, and Material Map Prep or intentionally scoped equivalents.

items.label: Changing Workflow changes the workbench layout.
items.detail: Select each available workflow and confirm the central panel changes appropriately rather than always showing the same candidate grid.

items.label: Selected phase/workflow persists across reopen.
items.detail: Select a non-default phase/workflow, close and reopen the window, and verify the selection returns or gracefully resets with a reason.

sections.title: Random Explore and candidate grid
sections.guidancePrompt: Validate the existing random-generation core and candidate-card interactions.

items.label: Generate creates a populated candidate grid.
items.detail: Run Generate. Confirm candidates draw with previews, labels, selection state, and no console errors.

items.label: Generation progress/stop state is clear.
items.detail: Start a larger generation if available. Confirm Generate disables or becomes Stop/Cancel and status/progress updates until complete.

items.label: Candidate selection and active candidate are clear.
items.detail: Click, Ctrl/Shift-select where supported, and confirm selected vs active candidate states are visually distinct and labelled/tooltipped.

items.label: Candidate card actions are reachable.
items.detail: Test Select/Guide-or-Lock/Edit/Duplicate/Delete/More actions that exist. Confirm actions update status and do not require obscure clicks.

items.label: Candidate edit overlay opens and edits the selected texture.
items.detail: Open candidate edit. Adjust blend/pattern/density/stamp controls. Confirm preview updates only after intended action or safe live update.

items.label: Candidate density/view setting visibly changes card density.
items.detail: Change texture/candidate density in View. Confirm card size/count per row changes, or mark fail if the control is decorative.

items.label: Candidate grid empty state is helpful.
items.detail: Clear candidates/session if possible. Confirm the empty state gives a safe primary Generate action and explains the next step.

sections.title: Manual Compose and layer controls
sections.guidancePrompt: Manual texture design should be a first-class workflow, not hidden helper code.

items.label: User can add a manual procedural layer/base.
items.detail: In Manual Compose or equivalent, use Add Layer. Confirm a new layer appears with preview and editable settings.

items.label: Layer stack/base grid is visible and practical.
items.detail: Check layer cards/list wrap or scroll cleanly. Enable/solo/lock/randomize/menu controls should be readable and not cramped.

items.label: Selected layer editor is reachable.
items.detail: Select a layer and edit blend, pattern, density, stamp, source, and advanced fields through the intended contextual surface.

items.label: Layers can be reordered.
items.detail: Drag or use menu actions to reorder layers. Confirm combined preview changes and state persists.

items.label: Layer duplicate and delete are safe.
items.detail: Duplicate a layer, delete it, and confirm Undo support if implemented or clear confirmation/status if not.

items.label: Generated candidate can be added as a layer.
items.detail: From a candidate card/menu, use Add as Layer/Bake Source/Edit Recipe equivalent. Confirm it appears in Manual Compose.

items.label: Manual composition has a combined output preview.
items.detail: Adjust at least two layers with different blend modes and confirm the combined texture preview updates correctly.

sections.title: Guide, preserve, similarity, and influence generation
sections.guidancePrompt: Validate the middle ground between random generation and hard locking.

items.label: User-facing labels distinguish Guide, Preserve, Similarity, and Mutation.
items.detail: Check toolbar, cards, inspector, and status messages. Prefer Use as Guide over ambiguous Lock unless lock truly means hard preservation.

items.label: Selected candidates can become generation guides/influences.
items.detail: Mark one or more candidates as guides, generate again, and confirm they move to or appear in the influence/guide shelf as intended.

items.label: Guide strength/influence weight is editable.
items.detail: Adjust guide strength on a candidate or guide tile. Confirm next generation and diagram/status reflect the new value.

items.label: Similarity target affects mutation radius.
items.detail: Generate with low similarity and high similarity from the same guide. Confirm high similarity produces closer variants.

items.label: Trait preserve chips affect output by trait.
items.detail: Preserve Structure/Tone/Seam or available equivalents, generate, and compare results. Mark partial if controls exist but effect is unclear.

items.label: Guides can be removed or cleared safely.
items.detail: Remove one guide and clear all guides. Confirm no stale references remain and random generation resumes.

items.label: Status text explains what will happen next.
items.detail: Before pressing Generate, the UI should state whether generation is fresh, guided, preserved, or similarity-targeted.

sections.title: Texture-native influence diagrams
sections.guidancePrompt: The influence section should explain how actual textures affect the next generation.

items.label: Random Explore shows a Texture Influence Quilt or equivalent.
items.detail: With guides active, inspect the influence diagram. It should show source-to-trait-to-output relationships, not only a list of thumbnails/sliders.

items.label: Influence textures are embedded in trait lanes.
items.detail: Check Structure, Density, Tone, Colour, Detail, Scale, Blend Order, and Seam lanes. At least key lanes should use processed strips/maps from source textures.

items.label: Hovering a source or trait highlights related contributions.
items.detail: Hover source textures and trait lanes. Confirm related segments highlight and unrelated content dims or is clearly separated.

items.label: Clicking a trait segment opens useful details.
items.detail: Open a trait/source overlay. Verify guide strength, similarity, preserve mode, source channel, or related controls are available without wall-of-fields clutter.

items.label: Diagram shows next-generation mutation/similarity envelope.
items.detail: Confirm the diagram visually communicates close/balanced/loose exploration and updates when Mutation or Similarity changes.

items.label: Conflicting guides are indicated clearly.
items.detail: Use guides with visibly different tone/density/scale. Confirm conflicts are labelled with text/icon/tooltip, not colour alone.

items.label: Diagram has compact and expanded behavior.
items.detail: Resize the window and/or open expanded influence details. Confirm compact mode remains informative and expanded mode avoids unreadable clutter.

items.label: Feature previews are cached, not regenerated per repaint.
items.detail: Interact, resize, and move the mouse over the diagram while watching responsiveness and Console. No allocation spikes or repaint-driven errors should appear.

sections.title: Guided Refine, Blend Lab, Reference Match, and Constraint Match
sections.guidancePrompt: Test advanced generation workflows where implemented; mark missing workflows as fail or not implemented.

items.label: Guided Refine uses a focused target texture layout.
items.detail: Select a target candidate and open Guided Refine. Confirm the active texture is central, with similarity/preserve controls nearby.

items.label: Similarity Ring communicates per-trait closeness.
items.detail: Check whether Structure/Tone/Density/Colour/Detail/Blend/Seam sectors show preservation strength around the active texture.

items.label: Blend Lab allows selecting Texture A and Texture B.
items.detail: Pick two candidates/presets/references. Confirm A/B previews are visible and swappable.

items.label: Blend Lab exposes trait-specific A/B mixing.
items.detail: Adjust structure/tone/colour/detail/blend-order sliders or lanes. Confirm generated outputs reflect different source contributions.

items.label: Reference Match accepts a source/reference texture.
items.detail: Assign a texture asset. Confirm source preview, extraction controls, and safe missing/invalid texture messages.

items.label: Reference Decomposition Map shows extracted traits.
items.detail: Verify edge/structure, density/mask, tone/histogram, palette/ramp, seam/edge strips, and stamp/source extraction previews where available.

items.label: Constraint Match lets users define target constraints.
items.detail: Set tileable, coverage range, contrast, scale, tone, or map intent constraints using compact controls or overlay.

items.label: Constraint results are scored and sorted.
items.detail: Generate candidates and confirm score, seam, coverage, contrast, scale/tone metrics appear on cards or matrix rows.

sections.title: Presets, material maps, export, and history
sections.guidancePrompt: Validate production handoff and reuse flows.

items.label: Preset Browser uses a compact texture grid.
items.detail: Open Preset Browser. Confirm search/filter/sort and small cards with Use/Edit/Duplicate/Guide/More controls.

items.label: Selected preset shows recipe stack or useful preview.
items.detail: Select a preset/template. Confirm layers/blend steps/output preview are understandable before Use/Edit.

items.label: Checkerboard preview toggle has visible effect.

items.label: Seam guide or seam overlay is visible and useful.

items.label: Generate Seamless mode changes output behavior.

items.label: Stamps wrap across tile edges.
items.detail: Use large stamps near edges or high density settings. Confirm wrapped counterparts appear and tiled preview has fewer cutoffs.

items.label: Seam score or tileability status is reported.

items.label: Seam/tileability can be preserved in guided generation.
